personality_one_liner: A fresh, approachable lifestyle tracker that feels like a clean glass of water: bright, soft, fluid, and effortless.

spacing.rule: Generous spacing to ensure the app feels breathable and 'fluid'. Content never sits tight against edges.

do's: Apply to the bottom tab bar, floating quick-add buttons (if sticky), and sticky bottom sheet handles
Use heavy tint at 75%+ over active bright backgrounds to ensure crisp readable numbers and text
dont's: Do not blur standard list rows or static form fields
Do not blur the main circular progress indicator; it should remain highly legible

screens.name: Auth
screens.purpose: A seamless entry point featuring a calm water-inspired visual and simple auth options.

states.loading: Gentle fluid spinner in brand color
states.error: Soft error toast matching the friendly aesthetic, never aggressive

screens.layout: Full-bleed abstract minimal aqua gradient background. A bottom sheet or bottom-aligned white card houses the login controls (Email/password + Google auth). Large touch targets, pill-shaped inputs.

screens.name: Home
screens.purpose: The primary dashboard focused entirely on immediate visual feedback of hydration and one-tap logging.

states.loading: Pulsing skeleton of the circular ring and quick-add pills
states.empty: A clean glass of water illustration hinting to log the first drink
states.error: Retry block overlaid if fetching history fails

screens.layout: Top section: Large, thick circular progress ring displaying volume (e.g., '1200 ml') and goal ('of 2000 ml'). Mid section: Horizontal scrollable row of pill-shaped quick-add buttons (+100ml, +250ml, etc.) colored in brandTertiary for touchability. Bottom section: A clean, rounded white card containing a scrollable history log of today's intake.

screens.name: Reports
screens.purpose: Provides a comprehensive bento-grid view of the user's habits, weekly trends, and monthly momentum.

states.empty: Friendly illustration encouraging user to log for a few days to generate insights
states.error: Simple retry button within the main graph card

screens.layout: Bento-style layout. Top: KPI summary cards (streak, total tracked). Middle: Weekly progress bar chart displaying daily volume vs target. Bottom: Monthly achievement calendar using a heat-map dot-grid (each day color-coded based on target achieved/partial/none).

screens.name: Reminders
screens.purpose: Manages hourly nudges with frictionless, playful toggles.

states.empty: A sleeping water drop icon with a prompt to enable reminders

screens.layout: Large master toggle at the top. Below: Soft rounded cards for interval selection (e.g., Every 1h, 2h), active start/end time pickers. Bottom: Quick-pause action pills (Pause 30m, 1h, until tomorrow).

screens.name: Profile & Settings
screens.purpose: Account management and tracker customization, keeping settings warm and uncomplicated.
screens.layout: Top: User details and Target Calculator (weight/activity inputs). Middle: Separated soft cards for unit preferences (ml/liter), app theme, and the CSV Export action button. Single-column list layout with md gaps.

auth_background.alt: Soft minimal aqua blue abstract gradient

home_empty_state.alt: Clean drinking glass filled with water in fresh sunlight

reports_hero_backdrop.alt: Abstract water splash waves on a dark background, heavily tinted for contrast

instructions_to_main_agent: CRITICAL: The prompt specifically requested 'fresh & minimal aqua/blue', which overrides the global blue/navy ban. Stick exactly to the provided cyan/aqua/sky-blue palette.
Implement the home screen with a large, central circular progress ring for the daily target. It should visually anchor the screen.
Use horizontal scroll views for the quick-add buttons (e.g., +100ml, +250ml) styled as large, touchable pills.
Ensure all cards have soft rounding (lg radius = 20) to match the tactile/playful personality, but maintain a clean, uncluttered layout so it feels minimal.
For the Reports screen, build a 'bento box' layout. The monthly calendar should be a dot-grid/heatmap where color intensity signifies achievement level.
Ensure haptics are wired to all quick-add buttons and toggles to make the app feel responsive and physical.
Do not use generic 'AI' icons; use Phosphor icons with rounded/filled variants that align with the soft aesthetic.
Always place a gradient scrim layer between images and text (e.g., on the Auth background screen) to maintain a >= 4.5:1 contrast ratio.
